evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012
evidence.field: 車部 entry; PDF p.1260, printed p.1245; scan /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-1260/source.png; inspected original pixels, including the 車 headword, historical-form rows, and paragraph
evidence.text: The entry is headed 車(车), gives the readings chē and a traditional phonological classification, and labels 車 a 形聲字. It quotes 說文’s account of 車 as the collective name for vehicle body and wheels and as pictographic, then discusses changing depictions: some oracle-bone and late Shang/early Zhou bronze forms omit features, and a reduced form is analyzed as a wheel-and-axle depiction. Its forms row includes oracle-bone, bronze, 說文 small-seal, regular 車, and regular 车. The book’s account is a distinct, more detailed analysis than a simple uniformly pictographic description; retain attribution and the book’s stated uncertainty around individual forms.
evidence.title: 字源 (2012 edition; inspected PDF page 1260, printed page 1245)

evidence.text: The database describes oracle forms of 車 as variable depictions of vehicle features, including wheels, body/framework, crossbar and yoke; later forms select features and develop toward regular 車. This supports a pictographic graphic history, though the book’s more specific account of a reduced form as wheel-and-axle is not independently established by this summary.
evidence.title: 漢字「車」：字形演變

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: oracle-bone and bronze uses; graphic description
evidence.text: The database describes variable oracle and bronze forms that may show wheels, body, axle, yoke, pole and crossbar. It identifies oracle-bone examples Heji 11452 for vehicles (“six vehicles”), Heji 11450 for 車馬, and Heji 584 as a place-name use; bronze examples include vehicle and war-chariot uses. These are the database’s readings of cited inscriptions; it does not give calendar dates for those individual examples.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 車

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Concised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
evidence.field: 車 current Mandarin reading and senses
evidence.text: The inspected entry gives chē and lists vehicle, machinery using rotating axles, machine sewing/cutting, and a cartload measure without marking these senses obsolete or restricting them to historical quotations. This supports current lexicographic status for these senses, but does not date their semantic development.

evidence.text: The official Unihan record for U+8ECA lists kMandarin chē, kHanyuPinyin chē,jū, and simplified variant 车. This is current character metadata, not evidence for an ancient sound relationship or a historical explanation of simplification.

evidence.source: 国务院《汉字简化方案》, transcribed at Wikisource
evidence.text: The resolution states the first table of 230 simplified characters was to be used in printed and handwritten documents from 1 February 1956. This supports the standardization date, not the origin of the earlier cursive form. The official Ministry page was located in search but opening it failed with a redirect loop; the inspected text here is the Wikisource transcription.

The book’s claims about reduced forms and the particular wheel-and-axle interpretation are the author’s analysis; the inspected external summaries support variable pictorial forms and reduction but do not independently settle the identification of every reduced historical shape.

The contemporary MOE entry inspected was Traditional Chinese 車. A verified official Unicode entry supplies 车’s kMandarin reading but not its current dictionary sense; current simplified-form sense documentation was not separately opened.

The BNU URL cited in the supplied dossier resolves to an unrelated essay in this inspection, so no Sui-or-earlier date for cursive 车 is independently verified here. The 1956 standardization claim is supported only by the inspected transcription after the official Ministry page failed to open.
